subject: A very simple question re: bolding axis titles

messages.author: 9cbdcb011f8600fa
messages.subject: A very simple question re: bolding axis titles
parts:
Hi all, 

I am banging my head against my computer for the simplest task. When making a simple scatterplot, I am able to label my x and y axes with bold font, as well as the axis labels. I am using basic R coding, not ggplot. 
 
I have two similar but different issues regarding bolding font of labels/titles: 

1) I cannot get my legend title font to bold in the first graph. I have tried things like main.font = 2, and title.font = 2, to no avail. 

2) My axis titles and axis labels will not bold in the boxplot (the second graph). 

Here is my code: 

#SCATTERPLOT AP.HEAD ~ HECTARES
plot(All.SRs.Head$AP.Head ~ All.SRs.Head$Hectares, col= All.SRs.Head$Scale, pch=22, bg = All.SRs.Head$Scale, 
     main = "Response Ratio of RG:CG, Animal Productivity/Head (kg) ~ Study Size (Hectares)", 
     ylab = "RR of Animal Productivity/Head (kg)", 
     xlab = "Study Size (ha)", font.axis = 2, font.lab = 2)
legend("bottomright", cex = 1, inset=.01,c("Ranch","Research"), border = c("black","red"), 
       fill = c("black","red"), text.font = 2, horiz=FALSE, title = "Study Size (Scale)")
abline(h=1, col="red") 
abline(lm(All.SRs.Head$AP.Head ~ All.SRs.Head$Hectares))

#BOXPLOT AP.HEAD ~ SCALE
plot(All.SRs.Head$AP.Head ~ All.SRs.Head$Scale, col=c("red","darkgrey"), names=c("Ranch","Research"), 
     main = "Response Ratio of RG:CG, Animal Productivity/Head (kg) ~ Study Size (Scale)", 
     ylab = "Response Ratio of RG:CG, Animal Productivity/Head (kg)", 
     xlab = "Study Size (Scale)", font.axis = 2, font.lab = 2)


Thank you for any suggestions! I apologize in advance if I left out important information. Thanks!

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: A very simple question re: bolding axis titles
parts:
I'd try using "plotmath":

?plotmath

In this instance:

title = expression(bold("Study Size (Scale)"))

-- Mike

messages.author: 1bd043dc49f3e3c4
messages.subject: Re: A very simple question re: bolding axis titles
parts:
Hi Kristina,
Have you tried pulling out your axis labels separately using axis() and then try using font.lab, font.axis and font.main?

You may have looked already, but par() has most of the details on the font() options.

as snippets to try:
plot(x, y, 
font.main=3, main="title")

Alternatively you could set the font to something you want to use first, then plot your legend, then reset:
op.default<-par() # the default settings
op.new<-par(font=2, font.sub=2, family="serif", font.main=2) # the settings you want

legend(...)  # your plot
axis(...)

par(op.default) # reset to default, or alternatively just use dev.off() and it will reset
 

Hope that helps!

R

Thank you Ryan, 

Yes I have tried pulling out the axis labels separately, and tried font.main/etc. in the plot function, to no avail. 
Can you give an example of how I might do that? I found something online like that, but could not make it work, so I am clearly doing something wrong in that respect. The labels end up looking really funky (completely illegible with thousands of numbers stacked on top of each other, even after suppressing the original axes), and the axis tick marks are not correct. Here is an example of one attempt: 
axis(1, at = All.SRs.Head$Scale, labels = All.SRs.Head$Scale, las = 2, )
axis(2, at = All.SRs.Head$AP.Head, labels = All.SRs.Head$AP.Head, las = 2, )

The second suggestion does a beautiful job on regular scatterplots and also the legend (YES!!) but still does not work for the boxplot (same problem I have been having already remains) axis labels or tick marks. 

​Mike, thank you for your suggestion as well. I am not able to get that function to work, but do not believe I am applying it correctly. However, the legend title is no longer a problem, as Ryan's suggestion worked for that little issue. Would your potential solution apply to the axis labels too? 
​
​Thank you again for all of your help, and I apologize in advance for my denseness and confusion. ​

~ Kristina

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Re: A very simple question re: bolding axis titles
parts:
Hi, Kristina. I think the plotmath thing will work any (? Vince
probably knows for sure ;-) place. I've attached a file, "bold.R",
that shows the plotmath/bold function used in the first of your two
original examples and in a boxplot example from some notes I wrote
about R for a class. The technique is pretty straightforward:
wherever you have:

param="some text"

you just replace it with:

param=expression(bold("some text"))

Note that as I didn't have access to your data set, I substituted the
"mtcars" data set, just to get something that would actually run.

My boxplot example is at the end of the file, after the line that says:

######################## MH boxplot example begins here

If you look at the specification of "xlab" in that example, you'll see
that it uses the trick mentioned above, and it *did* make the labels
bold when I ran it on my machine.

-- Mike
